_comment: Everything on the site that is not a project or a service. IMPORTANT: nothing in `proof` is invented. testimonials, clients and stats all start empty, and the site shows the `expectations` module instead of social proof until you fill them in. Only add a testimonial you actually received, and only add a stat you can back up.

expectations.title: How the work is made
expectations.lede: No testimonials here yet — so instead, exactly what you get when you hand a brand over.

items.title: Thinking, not just files
items.text: Every direction arrives with the reasoning behind it: what it says about your business, and why it beats the obvious version of itself.

items.title: Tested before it's shown
items.text: Marks get checked small, in one colour, and reversed on dark before you ever see them. If it only works on a moodboard, it doesn't ship.

items.title: Files your printer accepts
items.text: Vector sources, correct colour values, bleed where it belongs. Nothing to re-export a week later because a file opened wrong.

items.title: One person, start to finish
items.text: Whoever reads your brief draws the work and delivers it. Nothing is handed off, outsourced or lost in translation.

process.title: Four stages, and what each one asks of you
process.lede: Design goes wrong when nobody says who is responsible for what. Here it is, in order.

steps.name: Brief
steps.summary: We agree on what is being made before anything is drawn.
client: What the business does, and who it is for
Two or three brands you admire — and one you don't
Any existing assets: old logos, colours, fonts, photography
Where the brand has to appear (signage, packaging, app, print)
studio: A written read-back of the brief so nothing is assumed
Questions on anything ambiguous, before work starts

steps.name: Direction
client: Pick the direction that feels most like the business
Say what is and isn't working, in plain words — no design vocabulary needed
studio: Distinct directions, each one a genuine alternative rather than a colour variation
The rationale behind each: what it signals and to whom

steps.name: Craft
steps.summary: The chosen direction gets built properly.
client: Consolidated feedback in one pass, so revisions stay coherent
studio: Construction, optical corrections, spacing and scale testing
Colour, type and secondary elements resolved into a system
Application mockups so you can see it in the world, not on a white square

steps.name: Handover
steps.summary: Everything you need to use the brand without me.
client: Confirm the final files open correctly on your side
studio: Every file format the deliverables list promised
Guidelines covering usage, spacing, colour and misuse (on guideline projects)
A walkthrough of what is in the folder and when to use each file

brief.title: Tell me about your brand.
brief.lede: The first message decides how fast this moves. Six lines is enough — send these and the reply comes back with a real answer instead of a questionnaire.

items.label: Business name
items.hint: And what it does, in one sentence.

items.label: Industry
items.hint: Plus who the customer is, if it isn't obvious.

items.label: What you need
items.hint: Logo, full guidelines, stationery, social, animation — or say you're unsure.

items.label: Timeline
items.hint: A launch date or a deadline, if there is one.

items.label: References
items.hint: Two or three brands you like, and ideally one you don't.

items.label: Existing assets
items.hint: Old logo, colours, fonts, photography — anything already in use.

reassurance: Not sure what you need? Say so — scoping the right service is part of the first reply.
Everything runs through Fiverr: the brief, the previews, the revisions and the final files stay in one thread.
Payment and delivery are handled by Fiverr's own order system, not by me.
brief.ctaNote: Opens Fiverr in a new tab. No account? Signing up takes a minute.
